method: After a sealed question-only derivation and explicit phase-two authorization, I read the complete authored QA, scoped declarations and source bindings, frozen plan, seal and authorization for the three C items. I reproduced the raw and canonical payload digests, question digests, freeze and phase-one seals, source-file and declaration-span hashes, and checked the target/support identifiers and local graph dependencies. I compared the reference, all rubric rows and partial-credit pathways, error/alternative entries, every map node and join, and the edge cases to the sealed arguments. Small independent enumerations provided extra checks of the signs and degeneracies. This is an independent mathematical packet review within the stated candidate and public-use scope; empirical difficulty, corpus-wide deduplication and formal re-execution are outside its evidence. For the version-two re-review I compared the archived report and C3s payload with the newly authorized bytes. I checked the sole changed field against the sealed sector computation, the reference, R5 and N10, and reverified the full raw and canonical payload bindings and question hashes for every slot.

items.semantic_core_verdict: Accept as a finite, input-column-weighted circuit identity. The general product comes from the pinned multiplication law. The defining work specific to this candidate is transporting the diagonal, distinguishing exact from projective agreement over the full state space, and diagnosing the resulting coherent failure on the given two-bit wiring. Its declared exposure to pullback and relative-phase problems is apt; the scoped review makes no corpus-wide uniqueness claim.
items.reasoning: The answer reads the later table at p(x) and places the output at q(p(x)), then compares the sole supported output in each column to force the input table f∘p. The condition f∘p=f is precisely constancy on each orbit. With the stated orientation D_f P_p=λ P_p D_f, the finite unit table admits λ exactly when every ratio f(p(x))/f(x) agrees across all labels. The real-angle specialization gives ratios (1,1,exp(iθ),exp(−iθ)); the stationary columns force λ=1, so both kinds of equality occur exactly at θ∈2πℤ. At π the two signs on the balanced |00⟩,|10⟩ input give inner product zero after routing to |00⟩,|11⟩, while all single-input distributions are identical. I checked the three boundary rows individually, including the fixed-point and unspecified between-cycle exact phases, as well as all five listed errors. Enumerating all 384 combinations of three-label permutations and fourth-root tables reproduced the general exact and common-ratio tests.

items.rubric_assessment: R1 through R5 each carry two points, totaling ten. They respectively credit the coefficient and label, the unique pullback and exact equality, a consistent global scalar with both implications, the complete two-bit table and angles, and a verified witness with the basis-probability explanation. The one-point clauses cover relevant incomplete pieces. Entrywise multiplication, conjugation, ket evaluation, a common-λ cycle argument including closure, and either orientation of the scalar can earn full credit. Every balanced pair with one basis ket from each control sector works at π, including with a relative input phase. The relative-unitary witness therefore also qualifies.
items.map_assessment: I checked all nine nodes and both alternative routes. N1 carries the general column action with the question's unit hypothesis, N2 composes, and N3 specializes the composition to diagonal transport. N4 and N5 branch into exact and common-scalar tests. The separate two-bit input at N6 supplies routing and target data. N7 joins N3 with N6 to find the ratios, N8 joins N4/N5/N7 to test angles, and N9 joins unit column support at N1 with the signed N7 ratios to prove the coherent witness and the basis distribution. The declared premises precede their dependents. Conjugating a diagonal and examining the relative unitary are valid alternative routes under the stated hypotheses.
limitations: Global phase applies to the full operator. A cyclewise root-of-unity closure condition alone does not decide whether a supplied table has constant ratios. The author instead tests every column.
The controlled NOT is involutive, so its wiring example alone cannot distinguish f∘p from f∘p⁻¹. The general proof does distinguish them.

items.semantic_core_verdict: Accept as an exact, label-preserving diagonal-conjugation problem for the same permutation. The semantic core is the classification by labeled cycle products and transport between prescribed vertex phases, including construction of every calibration and the freedom on each component. This goes beyond the frozen weighted-composition theorem and ordinary phase-free permutation conjugation.

Iterating on directed arcs gives the full closed product test and η_t=R(s,j)η_s for pins on one cycle. Once closure is imposed, a base reference compared with every other pin is equivalent to checking all directed pairs, including paths that cross the base. The construction verifies the last edge, all prescribed pins, unit modulus and exactness. The recurrence proves all solutions are exhausted. One arbitrary phase survives on each unreferenced cycle; any prescribed pin fixes that cycle completely if its other constraints pass. A fixed point requires equal edge weights. The author and I both found the valid two-cycle assignments (1,1) and (−1,−1), total one, obstructed by prescribing both endpoint phases equal to one. I checked the four boundary rows and five common errors, and compared construction with enumerated fourth-root solutions over all 8,000 ratio/reference configurations on a fixed point and transposition.

items.map_assessment: I checked the nine nodes, all joins and both alternative routes. N1 supplies the shared routing and N2 supplies the unit diagonal and pins. Their join N3 derives the oriented ratio. Iteration at N4 branches into full-loop consistency N5 and pin-path consistency N6. N4/N5/N6 join at N7, where the path builds vertex phases, closure verifies the final edge, and the reference condition is vacuous for a cycle with no pins. limitations: The classification treats product equality on the same labeled cycle. Equal-length cycles cannot exchange labels under a diagonal calibration.
With a single reference the closed product remains a condition; there is no additional pairwise check. Ratios and conjugations use the nonzero modulus-one assumptions.

items.semantic_core_verdict: Accept as an inverse problem for exact complex traces of powers of a single weighted, known, labeled permutation. Its specific content is triangular recovery for distinct lengths, a genuine collision between different within-length multisets, and recovery with multiplicity and label-assignment boundaries using projected traces. The matrix and multiplication declarations supply the starting action rather than a formal proof of these inverse claims.
items.reasoning: The reference obtains the same n-step product as the sealed solution. A length L contributes L h_C^(n/L) only when L divides n, and its cyclic basis identifies the polynomial z^L−h_C with the required sign and degree. At each occurring distinct length the trace t_L contains one unknown term with coefficient L after shorter proper divisors are subtracted, and L≤N. I separately checked a length chain 1,2,4,8. The authored six-label example uses fixed products {1,−1} or {i,−i}; the two transposition products are {−1,1} or {1,1}. Both yield (z²−1)²(z²+1), so all traces agree with multiplicity. A direct computation gives a period of four with traces 0,2,0,6 in both assignments. My sealed example takes the common second transposition product to be i instead, confirming the ambiguity can also occur with distinct eigenvalues. In a length sector division by L yields exactly the first m_L power sums, which determine the monic product polynomial including repetitions. Every reassignment among equal-length cycles can be realized with a single weighted edge on each cycle; consequently labeled recovery is unique exactly for a constant multiset at that length. A check with three two-cycles of products 1,1,i reproduced the repeated-factor polynomial. The four boundary cases and six common errors are consistent with these arguments. The revised repeated-root boundary now says that the monic polynomial reconstructed from the first m_L projected power sums has a repeated root. This matches the independent repeated-root and constant-multiset checks, as well as R5 and N10, and resolves the earlier wording limitation.

items.rubric_assessment: Five two-point rows total ten. R1 credits returning labels and counted trace contributions and expressly admits an equivalent block calculation. R2 credits both cycle characteristic factors and their direct-sum product. R3 admits the stated recurrence or another proof with a computation and uniqueness. R4 accepts any realized six-label collision showing a changed multiset and agreement of all powers. R5 separates reconstruction with multiplicity from the label-assignment boundary. The alternative determinant, cyclic-vector and root-sum proofs, Newton followed by reciprocal-polynomial stripping for distinct lengths, and the arbitrary u,−u versus v,−v exchange with u²≠v² are correct. The generating-series or Newton solution for each sector and transport of the tables across equal-length cycles are also sound. The independent alternative collision qualifies for full R4 credit.

The unit-weight labeled permutation at N1 produces n-step walks at N2; N3 and N4 independently derive the characteristic and trace identities. N5 combines the known permutation with N4 in the explicitly conditional branch where lengths are distinct. In the general branch N6 constructs the six-label tables, and N3 and N6 join at N7 to prove the global obstruction. N8 supplies the separately stated measurement/identity hypotheses. N2 and N8 join at N9 for the scaled sector sums; N8 and N9 give the multiset at N10. N11 records realizability and invariance using N1/N4/N9, which joins reconstruction at N12 to obtain the exact uniqueness boundary. The distinct-length premise belongs specifically to N5, and does not enter the global counterexample or sector recovery.
limitations: The sector conclusions assume exact complex data and a known count of cycles. The labels at a length with one cycle or identical products are determined; individual labels remain interchangeable for unequal products.
